title: An interrupt in landing_lock between os.open of the lock file returning and the try that removes it leaves an empty lock file and an open descriptor
goal: landing_lock leaves no recordless lock file of its own behind on an interrupt at any point after it created the lock file, also right after os.open returned, before the block that removes the file opens; a lock file and a ticket stay readable by older code, and kb/_self/backlog.md says what the code covers

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_close
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", t], check=True)
path = str(bl_close.landing_lock_path(t))
real = os.open
def open_then_interrupt(p, *a, **k):
    fd = real(p, *a, **k)
    if str(p) == path:
        os.open = real
        raise KeyboardInterrupt
    return fd
os.open = open_then_interrupt
try:
    with bl_close.landing_lock(t, "ST-aaaaaaaa"):
        pass
except BaseException as e:
    print("interrupted by", type(e).__name__)
finally:
    os.open = real
print("lock file left behind:", os.path.exists(path))
sys.exit(0 if not os.path.exists(path) else 1)

gates.question: How does landing_lock make the lock file appear with its record?
options: write the record to a pid-named file beside the lock and os.link it to the lock path
keep os.open O_EXCL on the lock path and narrow the window with more handlers
gates.recommendation: write the record to a pid-named file beside the lock and os.link it to the lock path
gates.reason: the lock path never exists without its record, so no interrupt can leave an empty one, and os.link fails when the lock exists like O_EXCL
gates.answer: write the record to a pid-named file beside the lock and os.link it to the lock path

notes: From the SP-luspfajx review (G1). The window is the gap between os.open returning and the try after got = True; BG-z3cotvxq closed only the part after it. Any design is fine that leaves no file without a record (for example writing the record to a pid-named temp file and os.link-ing it to the lock path, then the finally removes a lock file whose record names this pid with or without got), as long as the lock file keeps its format (pid, clone, start, item lines) and an older process that polls the same path still reads it, clears a dead holder's file as before and never sees a half-written one. Check the same repro with the interrupt raised after os.link too. Run through bl_base.run_check: the repro uses a temp git repo only.
